clue.text: You or I say binding declaration

parts.note: 'you' and 'I' are examples of a pronoun, the 'say' marking them as examples
cement is a binding material that holds things together

explanation.surface: A grammarian insists that whatever you or I say counts as a binding statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public statement or announcement is a declaration, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Garlic-like plant that'd ramble across top of chestnut tree's trunk

indicators.note: the wandering word stretches across the single letter, so it is placed around it

parts.note: to ramble is to roam or wander aimlessly

indicators.note: the top of a word written downwards is its first letter

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a bulbous plant whose growth would sprawl over the crown of a chestnut's trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' has the wandering word straddle the top of 'chestnut'; 'that'd' is a link. The plant is an obscure one, so the trunk word helps confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocambole is sand leek, a European plant of the onion family closely related to garlic.

clue.text: Unpleasant return of an unpleasant spot

indicators.note: a return sends the little word back the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, is a filthy, unpleasant place

explanation.surface: An unpleasant spot on the skin has come back yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pimple coming back, but the spot is a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and unpleasant are plain synonyms, both describing something disagreeable.

clue.text: Just a kind of piano

definitions.meaning: just as an adjective means honest and fair, morally upstanding
a piano with its strings and frame set vertically rather than horizontally

explanation.definitionFit: An honest person is called upright, and a vertical household piano is an upright piano.

clue.text: Insensitive to phone the Guardian about nothing

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them
nothing is zero, written as the letter O
a Guardian setter calls the paper 'us', since it is the setter's own newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone is told that ringing the newspaper to complain over nothing is unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the paper this puzzle appeared in, so its setter can refer to it as 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: A callous person is hard-hearted and unfeeling, the same thing as insensitive.

clue.text: Chap to produce vegetable

parts.note: a chap is a man
to produce something, bring it forth, is to get it out

explanation.surface: A man is asked to bring a vegetable out for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout is a flat pea pod eaten whole, a green vegetable whose French name means 'eat all'.

clue.text: Bottom out at this point in a dirty clip?

indicators.note: a clip is a short piece cut from something longer, so the answer is a snippet of the words

explanation.surface: A film reaches its lowest point in a sleazy video excerpt.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a snippet of 'in a dirty'; 'out at this point' dresses the definition, the point where things bottom out.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, its bottom, as opposed to the zenith.

clue.text: With a subject, one has a boring fellow that's an expert in one

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the other pieces drill into the fellow and sit inside him

parts.note: a fellow is a man
thematic means having a theme or subject
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone with a specialism turns out to be a tedious person, and an authority in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring fellow' looks like a dull man, but 'boring' is the drilling; the 'one' in the definition refers back to the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'one' is a subject, mathematics, so an expert in that subject is a mathematician.

clue.text: Exploit group of cows left out in part of Ireland to get cleaner

parts.note: an exploit is a heroic deed, a feat
a herd is a group of cattle

indicators.note: out means the letter is excluded, dropped from the province's name

parts.note: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland

explanation.surface: A farmer exploits a herd in a corner of Ireland to make a tidy profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather duster is a household cleaning implement, a stick tipped with feathers.

clue.text: Lancaster comprised such a home for Gaunt's kin

definitions.text: such a home for Gaunt's kin

indicators.note: the letters of the name make up, or comprise, the answer when rearranged

explanation.surface: Lancaster was the family seat of John of Gaunt's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt was Duke of Lancaster, so the anagram fodder is itself his family's seat, making the clue nearly an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A family's ancestral home is the house handed down through generations of kin.

clue.text: Lacking cover to conceal tail of pig in poke

indicators.note: concealing means keeping inside, so the tail letter is held within

parts.note: nude means without clothes, uncovered

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A pig in a sack is naked but for hiding its tail, playing on 'a pig in a poke'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' puts G (the tail of 'pig') inside NUDE. A pig in a poke is an unseen purchase, a poke being a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke someone with an elbow is to nudge them, a gentle prod.

clue.text: Such taste is amateurish?

definitions.meaning: a flavour like that of cured pork

explanation.surface: Is a flavour like that a sign of an untrained cook?
explanation.definitionFit: Hammy describes a taste of ham, and overacting like an amateur 'ham' performer.

clue.text: See the world fall to pieces after high ball's taken in catch

indicators.note: after places the decay part behind the catch part
the ball is taken in, held inside the word for catch

parts.note: to catch is to get
a lob is a high ball in tennis or cricket
to rot is to decay and fall apart

explanation.surface: A cricketer's world collapses after a skied ball is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a cricket catch off a skied shot; 'high ball' is a lob.
explanation.definitionFit: To globetrot is to travel widely around the world, seeing it.

clue.text: May be seen nocturnally, if this fluid motion is out of line

indicators.note: the anagram is what is left when the line is taken out, so the line belongs inside it
fluid means flowing and changeable, so the word's letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Something is visible at night only if its smooth movement wanders off course.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer with its L taken out is an anagram ('fluid') of 'motion'; so put L back inside the reshuffled MOONIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moonlit is lit by the moon, so it is visible at night.

clue.text: Hit one protected by shell that's been taken off

annotationWithheld.why: Hit one protected by shell that's been taken off: LAM + ONE inside POD gives LAMPONED, one O short of LAMPOONED; the blog's parse has the same gap and no other piece supplies the O
annotationWithheld.clue: Hit one protected by shell that's been taken off

clue.text: Hold herb with maintained pull

indicators.note: maintained means kept or held, so the pull is held inside the herb

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb
to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: A recipe says to keep hold of the herb while pulling steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's hold is where cargo is stowed, and stowage is the space for storing it.

clue.text: A short bunny hop is more than enough

parts.note: bun is a short, dialect form for a rabbit or bunny
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A quick bunny hop is said to be plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: An abundance is a plentiful amount, more than enough of something.

clue.text: Heated exchange of "Hamlet" concerns king

indicators.note: an exchange swaps things around, so the letters change places

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from the Latin rex

explanation.surface: A heated argument in Shakespeare's play is about the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange of' rearranges HAMLET plus R; 'concerns' is the link. 'Heated exchange' looks like an argument, but 'Heated' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal means relating to heat, as in a thermal spring that is naturally heated.

clue.text: Unconscious reaction is to infiltrate former network

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside something, so the reaction slips inside the other word

parts.note: late can mean former, as in 'the late chairman'
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A reflex is said to infiltrate a former organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; the surface's 'Unconscious reaction' reads like a reflex, not a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework, a network of strips with gaps between.

clue.text: Shock regarding fund's initial loss

parts.note: as to means regarding or concerning

indicators.note: the initial loss is the first letter going missing from the word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked by money going missing from a fund at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to shock or amaze someone greatly.

clue.text: Almost tropical fruit?

indicators.note: fruit is the product of a plant, so the letters are produced in a new form; the question mark flags the double duty
almost the whole word means it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Is this fruit nearly from the tropics?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops L from 'tropical', and 'fruit?' rearranges TROPICA. The clue is an &lit: the apricot is a fruit not quite tropical.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a soft orange stone fruit grown in warm but not quite tropical climates.

clue.text: One moving forward goes around defensive position with dummy

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so the fort is held inside

parts.note: a comer is one who comes, advancing
a fort is a fortified defensive position

explanation.surface: A forward player circles a defensive line with a dummy pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is football or rugby, with a dummy as a feint pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A comforter is the British name for a baby's dummy, a rubber teat for sucking (a pacifier).

clue.text: Mum laps up good soft rock

indicators.note: to lap is to wrap around, so the word for mother goes round the good

parts.note: mama is another word for mum, mother

explanation.surface: Mother enjoys some good easy-listening music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laps up' puts G inside MAMA. 'soft rock' looks like a music genre, but it is molten rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten or semi-molten rock beneath the earth's surface.

clue.text: Not too bright to come back as cursed king

indicators.note: coming back means going backwards, so the dim word is read in reverse

parts.note: dim means not bright, in light or intelligence

explanation.surface: A rather dim figure returns as a doomed monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: King Midas was cursed so that everything he touched turned to gold.

clue.text: Somehow, I made the news channels

indicators.note: somehow suggests things worked out in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of somehow getting onto television news.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the means of mass communication, such as press and broadcasting news channels.

clue.text: Element that's central to monograph's circulation

indicators.note: circulation suggests going round, so the letters run backwards
central to means the letters come from the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A scholarly element is at the heart of how a monograph is distributed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central to' takes NOGRA from the middle of 'monograph's', and 'circulation' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a chemical element, a noble gas.

clue.text: Where detectives work on leads to each new crime, especially frequency

parts.note: in CID, the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

indicators.note: leads are first letters, the ones leading each word

explanation.surface: Detectives work on leads to each fresh crime, especially often.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police's plain-clothes detective branch, so a detective works IN CID; 'on' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidence is the rate at which something occurs, its frequency.

clue.text: Quietly goes off to side with Queen's vessel

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
addles means goes bad, as an egg goes off
a side is a team in sport
ER, Elizabeth Regina, abbreviates the Queen

explanation.surface: A quiet person leaves to stand beside the monarch's ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is a steam-driven vessel propelled by paddle wheels.
